post.description:
Invocation; validate input, run one version against it, validate output.
 An RPC error means the function did not produce a result: the request was
 rejected (unknown function, input violates the contract, no capacity) or
 the platform failed. Input violations are INVALID_ARGUMENT with one
 ContractViolation error detail each. If the function ran, the RPC
 succeeds and the response carries its output or a FunctionError. A
 function that raised, crashed or timed out, or a platform that could
 not run it, runs again up to the call's or the function's retries, with
 exponential backoff, while the call's deadline leaves room. An input
 that violates the contract never runs again.

connect-protocol-version.title: Connect-Protocol-Version
connect-protocol-version.description: Define the version of the Connect protocol

code.description: The status code, which should be an enum value of [google.rpc.Code][google.rpc.Code].

message.description: A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the [google.rpc.Status.details][google.rpc.Status.details] field, or localized by the client.

details.description: A list of messages that carry the error details. There is no limit on the number of messages.

type.description: A URL that acts as a globally unique identifier for the type of the serialized message. For example: `type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo`.

value.description: The Protobuf message, serialized as bytes and base64-encoded. The specific message type is identified by the `type` field.

debug.title: Debug
debug.description: Deserialized error detail payload. The 'type' field indicates the schema. This field is for easier debugging and should not be relied upon for application logic.

connect.error_details.Any.description: Contains an arbitrary serialized message along with a @type that describes the type of the serialized message, with an additional debug field for ConnectRPC error details.

inputSchema.title: input_schema
inputSchema.description:
input_schema and output_schema are Arrow schemas serialized as an IPC
 stream containing only the schema message, e.g. pyarrow's
 `schema.serialize()`.

functions.v1.ArrowContract.title: ArrowContract
functions.v1.ArrowContract.description:
ArrowContract types the boundary with Arrow schemas, for functions that
 operate on a batch of rows at a time. Input and output are one record
 batch each, as an Arrow IPC stream, on both the API and the function
 process's stdin/stdout. The output is row-aligned with the input: the same number
 of rows in the same order, so per-row bookkeeping the caller holds (such as
 an operation vector) applies to the output unchanged.

 Schemas are matched on field names, types and nullability; field metadata
 is ignored. A field the contract marks nullable accepts a non-nullable
 column.

functions.v1.Contract.title: Contract
functions.v1.Contract.description:
Contract is the typed I/O boundary of a function version. The platform
 enforces it on both sides: input before any compute is acquired, output
 before it is returned to the caller. It is a oneof so that other schema
 languages can be added later without changing FunctionSpec.

functions.v1.ContractViolation.title: ContractViolation
functions.v1.ContractViolation.description:
ContractViolation is one schema validation failure. instance_path and
 schema_path are JSON Pointers (RFC 6901) into the value and the schema.

secretValues.title: secret_values
secretValues.description:
secret_values are secrets to create for this version, variable name to
 value. Each is stored under the tenant as a new secret of its own, so a
 later version never changes what this one reads, and named in
 spec.secrets.

timeoutMs.title: timeout_ms
timeoutMs.description:
timeout_ms, max_concurrency and resources are as on Function. Zero
 values take the server defaults.

retries.title: retries
retries.description: retries is as on Function. Unset takes the default of 2.

functions.v1.CreateFunctionRequest.title: CreateFunctionRequest
functions.v1.CreateFunctionRequest.description:
CreateFunction creates the function and version 1 from spec. It returns as
 soon as the version is accepted, in BUILDING.

functions.v1.CreateFunctionVersionReques.title: CreateFunctionVersionRequest
functions.v1.CreateFunctionVersionReques.description:
CreateFunctionVersion adds a new immutable version. It becomes the
 function's current_version when it reaches READY.

timeoutMs.title: timeout_ms
timeoutMs.description:
timeout_ms bounds a single invocation's run time, measured from the
 moment input is handed to the function, whichever version runs.

maxConcurrency.title: max_concurrency
maxConcurrency.description:
max_concurrency is how many invocations of the function may run at once
 across every host. Invocations past it wait in the queue. 0 means no
 limit.

resources.title: resources
resources.description:
resources size the microVM every invocation of any version runs in. A
 change applies to the next invocation; each host snapshots the function
 again at the new size the first time it runs it.

retries.title: retries
retries.description:
retries is how many more times an invocation runs after its function
 raised, crashed or timed out, or the platform could not run it, with
 exponential backoff between attempts. A call may set its own.

network.title: network
network.description:
network is what the microVM can reach. A change applies to the next
 invocation, as resources do.

functions.v1.Function.title: Function
functions.v1.Function.description:
Function is a stable, named handle that callers invoke. It carries no
 behaviour of its own: current_version is the newest version that reached
 READY, and is what Invoke runs unless the caller pins a version. Lifecycle
 stamps are epoch millis; 0 means unset.

functions.v1.FunctionError.title: FunctionError
functions.v1.FunctionError.description:
FunctionError describes a function that ran and failed. type is the
 function-supplied error type, set for RAISED only; violations is set for
 OUTPUT_INVALID only.

functions.v1.FunctionErrorKind.title: FunctionErrorKind
functions.v1.FunctionErrorKind.description:
FunctionErrorKind classifies a failure attributable to the function rather
 than to the caller or the platform.

image.title: image
image.description:
image is an OCI reference, e.g. ghcr.io/galaxy-io/enrich-company:1.4.0.
 With source set it is the runtime the files land on, such as
 ghcr.io/galaxy-io/alchemy/runtime/python:3.13.

command.title: command
command.description:
command is the process to run, as an argv. Empty means the image's own
 Entrypoint + Cmd.

env.title: env
env.description:
env is added on top of the image's Env. Not for secrets: the values are
 part of the version and visible wherever it is.

secrets.title: secrets
secrets.description:
secrets names the tenant's secrets the function receives in its
 environment, variable name to secret name. The values are fetched by
 the host at invocation and never stored with the version.

source.title: source
source.description:
source makes the version a function built from source: files extracted
 over image under /app, where the runtime images look for the handler.

functions.v1.FunctionSpec.title: FunctionSpec
functions.v1.FunctionSpec.description: FunctionSpec is everything needed to build and run one version.

imageDigest.title: image_digest
imageDigest.description:
image_digest is the content digest (sha256:...) spec.image resolved to at
 build time. The version always runs this digest, even if the tag moves.

rootfsBytes.title: rootfs_bytes
rootfsBytes.description: rootfs_bytes is the size of the built root filesystem image.

buildLog.title: build_log
buildLog.description: build_log is the tail of the build's output, for FAILED versions mostly.

functions.v1.FunctionVersion.title: FunctionVersion
functions.v1.FunctionVersion.description:
FunctionVersion is an immutable, buildable version of a function. The
 contract is part of the version, so it never changes underneath a caller
 that pins one. version increases monotonically per function. Lifecycle
 stamps are epoch millis; 0 means unset.

functions.v1.FunctionVersionStatus.title: FunctionVersionStatus
functions.v1.FunctionVersionStatus.description:
FunctionVersionStatus is the lifecycle of the build that turns a spec into
 something bootable.

attempt.title: attempt
attempt.description:
attempt picks one attempt of the invocation, counting from 1. 0 is the
 latest.

functions.v1.GetInvocationLogsRequest.title: GetInvocationLogsRequest
functions.v1.GetInvocationLogsRequest.description:
GetInvocationLogs streams what an invocation's function wrote to stderr.
 With follow, the stream stays open while the invocation runs and ends when
 it does; without, it ends at what has been written so far.

functions.v1.GetInvocationLogsResponse.title: GetInvocationLogsResponse
functions.v1.GetInvocationLogsResponse.description:
GetInvocationLogsResponse is the next piece of the log, in order. Pieces
 are not split on line boundaries.

functions.v1.GetVersionResponse.title: GetVersionResponse
functions.v1.GetVersionResponse.description: GetVersionResponse is the build the server runs.

slots.title: slots
slots.description:
slots is how many invocations may hold a instance at once; slots_in_use
 is how many do right now.

memoryMibCommitted.title: memory_mib_committed
memoryMibCommitted.description: memory_mib_committed is the guest memory of all live instances.

functions.v1.Host.title: Host
functions.v1.Host.description: Host describes one host process and the machine it runs on.

functions.v1.Instance.title: Instance

functions.v1.InstanceStatus.title: InstanceStatus
functions.v1.InstanceStatus.description:
InstanceStatus is the live state of one microVM. Instances are not
 persisted: they die with the host process.

instanceId.title: instance_id
instanceId.description: instance_id names the microVM that served it, while it exists.

idempotencyKey.title: idempotency_key
idempotencyKey.description: idempotency_key is the caller's key, when the call carried one.

host.title: host
host.description:
host is the host the invocation was sent to, empty when none took
 it. Set by the server when it sends it and by the host in its record.

attempts.title: attempts
attempts.description: attempts is how many times a host has started to run it.

async.title: async
async.description: async is set when the caller did not wait for the result.

functions.v1.Invocation.title: Invocation
functions.v1.Invocation.description:
Invocation is the persisted record of one Invoke call. Lifecycle stamps
 are epoch millis; 0 means unset. started_at is when the function received
 its input, ended_at when the record reached a terminal status.

functions.v1.InvocationProtocol.title: InvocationProtocol
functions.v1.InvocationProtocol.description:
InvocationProtocol selects the ABI between the supervisor and the
 function process. Both are specified in docs/architecture.md.

functions.v1.InvocationStats.title: InvocationStats
functions.v1.InvocationStats.description:
InvocationStats breaks down where the time went, in microseconds, so the
 cost of each start path can be read directly off a response. acquire_us is
 from accepting the request to having a microVM ready to take input; run_us
 is from handing input to the function to receiving its result; total_us is
 the whole request as seen by the server, including both validations.

functions.v1.InvocationStatus.title: InvocationStatus
functions.v1.InvocationStatus.description: InvocationStatus is the persisted lifecycle state of an invocation.

functions.v1.InvokeAsyncRequest.title: InvokeAsyncRequest
functions.v1.InvokeAsyncRequest.description:
InvokeAsyncRequest is InvokeRequest for a caller that does not wait.
 idempotency_key returns the invocation an earlier call with the key
 queued instead of queueing another.

replayed.title: replayed
replayed.description:
replayed is set when an earlier call with the same idempotency_key
 queued invocation_id, and nothing was queued for this call.

functions.v1.InvokeAsyncResponse.title: InvokeAsyncResponse
functions.v1.InvokeAsyncResponse.description:
InvokeAsyncResponse is returned once the invocation is queued. Nothing
 waits for it to run and its output is dropped. GetInvocation follows its
 status, attempts and error.

idempotencyKey.title: idempotency_key
idempotencyKey.description:
idempotency_key makes the call safe to retry. Within the server's
 idempotency window, every call to the same function with the same key
 returns the invocation the first call started, with its output or
 error, instead of running again. The key is released, so that a retry
 runs, only when the platform never sent the invocation to a host. A
 call a host took but never reported on has an unknown outcome and holds
 the key: a retry gets ABORTED, and a new key runs again.

retries.title: retries
retries.description:
retries, when set, is how many more times this call runs after a failed
 attempt instead of the function's retries.

functions.v1.InvokeRequest.title: InvokeRequest
functions.v1.InvokeRequest.description:
Invoke runs a function synchronously. version 0 runs the function's
 current_version; any other value pins that version. input is opaque to the
 platform: the version's contract says what it must be (a JSON value for a
 JSON Schema contract, an Arrow IPC stream for an Arrow contract) and
 checks it before anything runs.

replayed.title: replayed
replayed.description:
replayed is set when the result is an earlier invocation's, found by
 the request's idempotency_key, and nothing ran for this call.

attempts.title: attempts
attempts.description: attempts is how many times the function ran for this result.

functions.v1.InvokeResponse.title: InvokeResponse
functions.v1.InvokeResponse.description:
InvokeResponse is returned whenever the function ran. output is the
 function's result in the encoding the contract defines, already checked
 against the output schema; error means the function ran and failed.
 version is the one that actually ran.

functions.v1.JsonSchemaContract.title: JsonSchemaContract
functions.v1.JsonSchemaContract.description:
JsonSchemaContract types the boundary with JSON Schema, draft 2020-12.
 Input and output are one JSON value each, on both the API and the function
 process's stdin/stdout. Each document must be self-contained: $ref may only
 point inside it.

hosts.title: hosts
hosts.description: Every host that has sent a heartbeat recently, by hostname.

functions.v1.ListInvocationsRequest.title: ListInvocationsRequest
functions.v1.ListInvocationsRequest.description:
ListInvocations returns newest first. Empty function_id lists the tenant's
 invocations across functions; empty statuses lists every status. since_ms
 (inclusive) and until_ms (exclusive) window on created_at; 0 means
 unbounded.

functions.v1.Network.title: Network
functions.v1.Network.description: Network is what a function's microVM can reach.

functions.v1.PaginationRequest.title: PaginationRequest
functions.v1.PaginationRequest.description:
PaginationRequest narrows a List response to one page. Absent means the
 full result. page_size is defaulted and capped server-side;
 cursor is an opaque token from a prior response, absent meaning the first
 page.

functions.v1.PaginationResponse.title: PaginationResponse
functions.v1.PaginationResponse.description:
PaginationResponse reports how many items matched before the page was cut,
 plus opaque cursors for the adjacent pages. Absent cursors mean no page in
 that direction.

functions.v1.Resources.title: Resources
functions.v1.Resources.description: Resources sizes the microVM. Zero fields take server defaults.

id.title: id
id.description: id names the runtime in a request, e.g. python.

label.title: label
label.description: label is the runtime's name for people, e.g. Python 3.13.

image.title: image
image.description: image is the reference a source spec sets as spec.image.

handlerPath.title: handler_path
handlerPath.description: handler_path is the file under /app the image runs, e.g. handler.py.

functions.v1.Runtime.title: Runtime
functions.v1.Runtime.description:
Runtime is an image a function built from source lands on, with what a
 client needs to offer it: the handler the image runs and a starter for it.

functions.v1.RuntimeStarters.title: RuntimeStarters
functions.v1.RuntimeStarters.description:
RuntimeStarters are handlers that read one input and write one output, per
 contract kind, for a function to start from.

functions.v1.Source.title: Source
functions.v1.Source.description:
Source is the files of a function built from source. A request carries
 their content; the server keeps them as an archive in the artifacts bucket
 and the version's spec names the archive and lists the files, with their
 content again on GetFunctionVersion. A spec that names an archive and
 carries no content, such as a version's own spec sent back to build it
 again, reuses the archive.

path.title: path
path.description: path is relative to /app, e.g. handler.py.

size.title: size
size.description: size is the content's length, set by the server.

sha256.title: sha256
sha256.description: sha256 is the archive's content digest, in hex.

functions.v1.SourceLayer.title: SourceLayer
functions.v1.SourceLayer.description: SourceLayer is the archive of a Source's files in the artifacts bucket.

functions.v1.StartKind.title: StartKind
functions.v1.StartKind.description: StartKind is how the microVM that served an invocation came to exist.

functions.v1.TailInvocationsRequest.title: TailInvocationsRequest
functions.v1.TailInvocationsRequest.description:
TailInvocations streams invocation changes. With should_replay the stream
 first emits every non-terminal invocation (each marked replay=true) so a
 reconnecting client is current before live events arrive.

functions.v1.TailInvocationsResponse.title: TailInvocationsResponse
functions.v1.TailInvocationsResponse.description:
TailInvocationsResponse is one lifecycle transition. event_type is the new
 status as a wire token (e.g. "running", "succeeded").

id.title: id
id.description: id names the template, e.g. call-decision-model.

runtime.title: runtime
runtime.description: runtime is the id of the Runtime the files run on.

jsonSchema.title: json_schema
jsonSchema.description:
json_schema and arrow are the source and sample contract for each
 contract kind; a client offers the one matching the contract it builds.

env.title: env
env.description: env are the variables the source reads, with their defaults.

secrets.title: secrets
secrets.description: secrets are the secrets the source reads, by variable name.

darkLockupUrl.title: dark_lockup_url
darkLockupUrl.description:
dark_lockup_url and light_lockup_url are the logo and name of the service
 the source calls.

timeoutMs.title: timeout_ms
timeoutMs.description:
timeout_ms and retries are the function settings the source needs. Each
 call costs money, so a template does not retry by default.

functions.v1.Template.title: Template
functions.v1.Template.description:
Template is a function to build from: its source, a sample contract and the
 settings the source needs.

functions.v1.TemplateSource.title: TemplateSource
functions.v1.TemplateSource.description:
TemplateSource is a template's handler and sample contract for one contract
 kind.

functions.v1.UpdateFunctionRequest.title: UpdateFunctionRequest
functions.v1.UpdateFunctionRequest.description:
UpdateFunction changes a function's settings. They apply to the next
 invocation of any version. timeout_ms, max_concurrency, resources,
 retries and network change only when set.

google.protobuf.ListValue.description: A JSON array whose elements may be any JSON value.

google.protobuf.NullValue.title: NullValue
google.protobuf.NullValue.description:
Represents a JSON `null`.

 `NullValue` is a sentinel, using an enum with only one value to represent
 the null value for the `Value` type union.

 A field of type `NullValue` with any value other than `0` is considered
 invalid. Most ProtoJSON serializers will emit a `Value` with a `null_value`
 set as a JSON `null` regardless of the integer value, and so will round trip
 to a `0` value.

google.protobuf.Struct.description: A JSON object whose property values may be any JSON value.

google.protobuf.Value.description: Any JSON value: `null`, number, string, boolean, array, or object.

metrics.v1.AggregateRow.title: AggregateRow
metrics.v1.AggregateRow.description: AggregateRow.values[i] is request.metrics[i] for this group.

metrics.v1.GetQueueRequest.title: GetQueueRequest
metrics.v1.GetQueueRequest.description:
GetQueueRequest narrows the counts to function_ids, or every function of
 the tenant when empty.

queued.title: queued
queued.description:
queued is invocations waiting to start: in the queue, or taken by a host
 that is building the function or waiting on its max_concurrency.

metrics.v1.Metric.title: Metric
metrics.v1.Metric.description:
Metric is an aggregatable measure over invocations. COUNT and the byte
 metrics are sums. The duration metrics are means in milliseconds over
 invocations that recorded the phase (a zero column means the phase never
 happened, e.g. acquire on an errored call, and is excluded).

metrics.v1.MetricDimension.title: MetricDimension
metrics.v1.MetricDimension.description:
MetricDimension names an invocations column usable for grouping and
 filtering. STATUS and START_KIND values are the lowercase wire tokens
 ("succeeded", "cold_boot"); the id dimensions are UUIDs.

metrics.v1.MetricFilter.title: MetricFilter
metrics.v1.MetricFilter.description:
MetricFilter narrows a query to invocations whose dimension is one of
 values.

metrics.v1.MetricGranularity.title: MetricGranularity
metrics.v1.MetricGranularity.description: MetricGranularity is the bucket width for timeseries queries.

metrics.title: metrics
metrics.description:
metrics are computed together per bucket; point values align with this
 order positionally.

tzOffsetMinutes.title: tz_offset_minutes
tzOffsetMinutes.description:
tz_offset_minutes shifts bucket boundaries east of UTC so DAY buckets
 match the viewer's local calendar day.

metrics.v1.Timeseries.title: Timeseries
metrics.v1.Timeseries.description:
Timeseries.key is the group_by dimension's value. Points are dense: every
 bucket in [since_ms, until_ms) is present, zero-filled, ascending; all
 series of a response are index-aligned. When a filter covers the group_by
 dimension, one series per requested value is returned in request order.

metrics.v1.TimeseriesPoint.title: TimeseriesPoint
metrics.v1.TimeseriesPoint.description: TimeseriesPoint.values[i] is request.metrics[i] for this bucket.

tags.name: functions.v1.FunctionsService
tags.description:
FunctionsService is the control plane for typed, image-based functions:
 it registers functions and their versions, and runs them in microVMs.

tags.name: metrics.v1.MetricsService
tags.description:
MetricsService is a generic, read-only aggregation surface over
 invocations: two query primitives (bucketed timeseries, windowed aggregate)
 parameterized by metric and dimension enums. New metrics and dimensions
 are enum additions; the RPC surface never changes.
